title: Mango Granita
changes_from_base: Mango purée replaces the strawberries, and it is frozen in ice-cube trays and pulsed instead of scraped.
summary: A refreshing frozen treat made from fresh mango purée and lemon juice, perfect for a light summer dessert.

ingredients.item: ripe mango flesh (from about 2 mangoes), sliced

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Place 450 g mango flesh and 180 ml water in a blender or food processor. Pulse the mixture until it is completely smooth.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pass the purée through a fine sieve into a bowl. Discard any fibres that remain in the mesh.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Stir in 70 g caster sugar and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Mix well until the sugar has fully dissolved into the mango liquid.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pour the mixture into 2 ice-cube trays. Place them in the freezer for at least 2 h until the cubes are solid.

steps.title: Process
steps.text: Place one layer of frozen cubes into the food processor and pulse 10-12 times. Stop when there are no large chunks left and the texture is icy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the granita into chilled glasses and serve at once. Repeat the pulsing process for the remaining cubes as needed.

tips: Choose very ripe fruit for the best natural flavour and sweetness.
Ensure the sugar is completely dissolved before freezing to prevent a gritty texture.
Chill your serving glasses in the freezer beforehand to keep the granita from melting too quickly.
storage: Keep the cubes in a freezer bag for up to 1 week and pulse them in the processor just before serving.
